summary: In Greek mythology, Argeus (Ancient Greek Ἀργεύς) was a king of Argos in the Abantiad/Proetid line — son of Megapenthes and, in Pausanias' succession, father of Anaxagoras, in whose family's third the maddened women were cured and the kingdom was divided among Melampus, Bias, and Anaxagoras.
attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia, "Argeus of Argos" · CC BY-SA 4.0

sections.heading: Son of Megapenthes
paragraphs: Pausanias sets Argeus between Megapenthes and Anaxagoras in the Argive king-list that descends from Proetus. His son Anaxagoras' reign is the hinge of the Melampid settlement: after the Proetid women are cured, a third of the kingdom passes to Melampus and Bias while the native third remains with Anaxagoras' house.
Other Argei — the Pelopid who marries Hegesandra at Amyclae, Licymnius' son who falls with Heracles, the Danaid bridegroom — are distinct. The atlas id is the Proetid king of Argos alone.
